documents.unit: Faculty of Arts and Sciences, Office of Undergraduate Education (Harvard College)
documents.title: Generative AI Guidance
tiers: Maximally restrictive (no generative AI at any stage)
Mixed (disallowed unless otherwise stated per assignment)
Fully encouraging (encouraged with acknowledgement and citation)
documents.summary: The Harvard College Office of Undergraduate Education requires every instructor to tell students the course AI policy and post it on Canvas. It offers three sample policies (maximally restrictive, mixed, fully encouraging), advises against AI detectors, sets privacy limits and announces a lockdown exam browser.
documents.stance_why: The page says 'All faculty are required to inform students of the policies governing generative AI use' and lets faculty 'choose from among the below example policies' that run from 'maximally restrictive' to 'fully-encouraging'; it sets no stance itself and delegates to instructors with tiered templates.

units.why: The opening framing sentence says Harvard 'supports responsible experimentation' with generative AI while flagging privacy, copyright and integrity considerations; it states the institution's overall posture, so P56 (framework for responsible AI use), informs, permit.
units.anchor: Harvard supports responsible experimentation with generative AI tools
units.resolution_why: A coded actor all, B coded admin; the sentence is addressed to everyone using the tools, so all. Both coded P56 informs permit; B's topic 'privacy-data' is secondary, so A's topics are kept.

units.why: Faculty 'can find Respondus ... to use for in-person seated exams and quizzes to ensure that students do not use AI'; this is an exam-time enforcement option that keeps AI out of assessments, so P22, instructor, may, restrict.
units.anchor: ensure that students do not use AI unless the course asks them to do so
units.policy: Starting in Fall 2025, faculty can use the Respondus browser lockdown tool on Canvas for in-person seated exams and quizzes to ensure that students do not use AI unless the course asks them to do so.
units.resolution_why: A wrote a normalized policy and B anchored the tool phrase with no policy; the anchor 'ensure that students do not use AI unless the course asks' states the purpose, but the permission to use the tool is in the full sentence, so the normalized policy is kept. Codes agreed.

units.why: 'All faculty are required to inform students of the policies governing generative AI use in class' is a duty on instructors to state a course AI policy, so P09, course-start, must.
units.anchor: All faculty are required to inform students of the policies governing generative AI use

units.why: 'you should post your policy on your Canvas site' tells instructors how to communicate the course AI policy, so P09, course-start, should.
units.anchor: you should post your policy on your Canvas site

units.why: Instructors 'can choose from among the below example policies ... or design your own to suit the needs of your course'; the choice of rule is left to the instructor, so P04, before-course, may.
units.anchor: You can choose from among the below example policies to add to your Canvas site
units.resolution_why: A coded P05 with a normalized policy, B coded P04. The sentence hands the choice to the instructor (P04); the naming of the three tiers is coded separately as P05 (next unit). Codes follow B.

units.why: The page labels three sample policies ('A maximally restrictive draft policy', 'A fully-encouraging draft policy', 'Mixed draft policy'), which are explicit tiers of AI use, so P05; it describes the offer rather than ordering anything, so informs.
units.anchor: A maximally restrictive draft policy:
units.policy: The page offers three draft course AI policies: maximally restrictive, fully-encouraging and mixed.
units.resolution_why: Only B coded the tiers as their own unit (A folded the tiers into its 'choose from' unit as P05). The tiers are a distinct fact from the choice rule and are real policy content, so kept; modality changed from B's may to informs because the sentence lists what is offered.

units.why: The sample text says 'We specifically forbid the use of ChatGPT or any other generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools at all stages of the work process', a ban on AI for the work, so P01, must-not, prohibit.
units.anchor: forbid the use of ChatGPT or any other generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools
units.policy: In the maximally restrictive sample policy, the use of ChatGPT or any other generative AI tools is forbidden at all stages of the work process, including preliminary ones.
units.resolution_why: Both coded P01 must-not prohibit. A's normalized policy is kept because the anchor omits 'at all stages of the work process, including preliminary ones'.

units.why: 'all work students submit for this course will be their own' makes students own what they submit, so P29, must.
units.anchor: all work students submit for this course will be their own

units.why: 'we expect for the assignment to list all team members who participated' requires students to name contributors on collaborative work. It sits inside the AI sample policy but is about attributing human collaborators, not AI use, and no type covers it.
units.anchor: we expect for the assignment to list all team members who participated
units.uncovered_note: Collaborative assignments must list all team members who participated (attribution of human contributors, not AI use).
units.resolution_why: A coded P29 (own work), B coded UNCOVERED. P29 is about owning what is submitted; naming team members is a different rule (attribution of human contributors), so UNCOVERED with a note. Topics follow A.

units.why: 'Violations of this policy will be considered academic misconduct' treats unauthorized AI use as misconduct, so P36, when-misuse. It repeats in all three sample policies and is coded once.
units.anchor: Violations of this policy will be considered academic misconduct.
units.resolution_why: A coded modality informs, B coded must and unit_stance restrict. The sentence binds students to a consequence, so must; it is a procedural consequence of the course policy rather than a position on AI use, so unit_stance neutral.

units.why: 'it is the student's responsibility to conform to expectations for each course' because 'different classes at Harvard could implement different AI policies'; each course governs itself, so P11, must.
units.anchor: it is the student's responsibility to conform to expectations for each course

units.why: 'This course encourages students to explore the use of generative artificial intelligence (GAI) tools ... for all assignments and assessments' welcomes AI by default, so P02, should, encourage.
units.anchor: This course encourages students to explore the use of generative artificial intelligence (GAI) tools
units.policy: In the fully-encouraging sample policy, the course encourages students to explore the use of GAI tools such as ChatGPT for all assignments and assessments.
units.resolution_why: Both coded P02 should encourage. The normalized policy is kept because the anchor omits 'for all assignments and assessments'.

units.why: 'Any such use must be appropriately acknowledged and cited' requires disclosure of permitted AI use, so P24, must.
units.anchor: Any such use must be appropriately acknowledged and cited.
units.resolution_why: A coded unit_stance require, B coded permit. The duty is a condition on permitted use, not a requirement to use AI, so permit.

units.why: 'It is each student's responsibility to assess the validity and applicability of any GAI output that is submitted' requires students to verify AI output, so P31, must.
units.anchor: student's responsibility to assess the validity and applicability of any GAI output

units.why: 'you bear the final responsibility' says the student owns what is submitted even when AI output is used, a rule distinct from the duty to check the output, so P29.
units.anchor: you bear the final responsibility
units.resolution_why: Only B coded this clause separately (A folded it into the validity unit). It is a distinct rule (ownership vs verification), so kept as P29; modality must because it binds the student, not informs.

units.why: 'The default is that such use is disallowed unless otherwise stated' bans AI by default with per-assignment exceptions, so P01, must-not, restrict.
units.anchor: The default is that such use is disallowed unless otherwise stated.
units.resolution_why: A coded P06 (fallback when silent), B coded P01. The sentence sets a default ban, not the rule for a silent syllabus, so P01 (default ban), restrict.

units.why: 'Certain assignments in this course will permit or even encourage the use of generative artificial intelligence (GAI) tools' sets AI permission assignment by assignment, so P04.
units.anchor: Certain assignments in this course will permit or even encourage the use of generative artificial

units.why: 'Visit the Bok Center for Teaching and Learning website for resources on teaching in the age of AI' points faculty to support for learning about AI in teaching, so P63.
units.anchor: resources on teaching in the age of AI
units.resolution_why: Only A found it. It is a real pointer to faculty support in the source, so kept; modality informs (a referral).

units.why: 'We should assume that all our students are proficient with these tools and should adjust our expectations accordingly' tells instructors to adapt expectations and assessment to AI, so P35, before-course, should.
units.anchor: We should assume that all our students are proficient with these tools and should adjust

units.why: 'A good first step is to feed representative assignments from your upcoming courses into a GAI tool' advises instructors to test assignments against AI before redesigning them, so P35, should.
units.anchor: feed representative assignments from your upcoming courses into a GAI tool such as ChatGPT
units.resolution_why: A coded P35, B coded P63 (faculty support). The advice is to test assignments against AI in order to adapt them, which is assignment redesign (P35), not training faculty to use AI.

units.why: 'decide on and disseminate a course-by-course policy on student use of GAI tools' leaves the rule to each course, so P04, before-course, should.
units.anchor: decide on and disseminate a course-by-course policy on student use of GAI tools

units.why: 'We also need to teach our students how to use these tools in an ethical and responsible manner' recommends teaching effective, responsible AI use, so P44, should.
units.anchor: teach our students how to use these tools in an ethical and responsible manner
units.resolution_why: A coded actor all and modality informs, B coded instructor and should. 'We ... need to teach' binds faculty and is a recommendation, so instructor, should.

units.why: 'It would be inadvisable to count on automated methods for GAI detection' tells instructors not to rely on AI detectors, so P39, should-not.
units.anchor: It would be inadvisable to count on automated methods for GAI detection.

units.why: 'FAS does not plan to provide/license such a tool for use in courses' says the faculty will not supply an AI detector, so P39, informs. The same sentence for proctoring tools is the next unit.
units.anchor: FAS does not plan to provide/license such a tool for use in courses.

units.why: 'FAS does not plan to provide/license' an internet-blocking exam-proctoring tool; it is a statement about what the institution will not supply for exams, which fits no type (P22 bans AI on exams; P33 shifts to proctored assessment).
units.anchor: technologies for exam proctoring that aim to block students from using the internet
units.policy: FAS does not plan to provide or license an exam-proctoring tool that blocks students from using the internet in courses.
units.uncovered_note: FAS does not plan to provide or license an internet-blocking exam-proctoring tool for courses.
units.resolution_why: Both coded UNCOVERED. A's normalized policy is kept; B's topics follow A.

units.why: 'No confidential information can be loaded into GAI systems, since there is no expectation of privacy or confidentiality' forbids entering confidential data, so P50, must-not, restrict.
units.anchor: No confidential information can be loaded into GAI systems
units.resolution_why: A coded phase during-work, B coded general. The rule is not tied to a course stage, so general.

units.why: 'Faculty must get documented permission from students before putting original student content into any generative AI tool' binds instructors on student data, so P50, must, restrict.
units.anchor: Faculty must get documented permission from students before putting original student content

units.why: 'students should be made aware of the risks of entering their original work into such tools' asks that students be told of the privacy risk, so P50, should; the addressee who must inform them is the instructor.
units.anchor: students should be made aware of the risks of entering their original work
units.resolution_why: Only B coded it. It is a distinct duty (inform students of the risk) in the same sentence as the faculty-permission rule, so kept; phase course-start because it is about communicating to students.

units.why: 'terms of service allow the company to access any information fed into it' states the data risk behind the privacy rule, so P50, informs.
units.anchor: terms of service allow the company to access any information fed into it

units.why: 'Harvard HUIT has compiled a list of available tools' points users to the institution's vetted tool list, so P50 (prefer vetted tools), informs.
units.anchor: Harvard HUIT has compiled a list of available tools
units.resolution_why: Only A coded it. It is a real statement of which tools are provided by the university, so kept; stance neutral.

units.why: 'Be sure to review Harvard's guidelines for use of these tools' directs users to the institutional guidelines, so P56, should.
units.anchor: Be sure to review Harvard's guidelines for use of these tools
units.resolution_why: Only B coded it. It is a real directive to follow the university guidelines, so kept.

units.why: 'the GAI responses will reflect the biases and inaccuracies that are contained in the training data' names a harm of AI output, so P53, informs.
units.anchor: the GAI responses will reflect the biases and inaccuracies that are contained in the training

units.why: 'Our challenge is to incentivize the level of engagement that leads to a deeper understanding' gives the learning rationale for the teaching response, so P41, informs.
units.anchor: incentivize the level of engagement that leads to a deeper understanding

units.why: 'some of the material they provide as factual are incorrect' states that AI output is often wrong, the basis for verifying it, so P31, informs.
units.anchor: some of the material they provide as factual are incorrect

documents.title: Teach with Generative AI
documents.summary: The university-wide Generative AI @ Harvard page is a faculty-facing resource on teaching with GenAI: course preparation, assessment redesign, risks and policies. It states that Schools let instructors customize AI policies if clearly communicated.
documents.stance_why: It says 'Schools within Harvard allow for the customization of AI usage policies by individual instructors, provided these are clearly communicated', so the page sets no student rule itself and delegates to schools and instructors.

units.why: 'Harvard has consistently tried to embrace new technology across our classrooms' states a welcoming institutional posture toward GenAI, so P02, informs, encourage.
units.anchor: Harvard has consistently tried to embrace new technology across our classrooms
units.resolution_why: A coded P56 (framework), B coded P02. The sentence is a welcoming stance, not a framework of rules, so P02. Actor all (general institutional statement).

units.why: 'free and open to all faculty, students and staff behind Harvard Key' describes university-provided AI tools available to students and staff, so P17, informs, permit.
units.anchor: free and open to all faculty, students and staff behind Harvard Key
units.resolution_why: A coded actor all, B coded admin; the access applies to all members, so all. Both coded P17 permit.

units.why: 'concerns about how they may compromise student assessments, promote academic dishonesty, and facilitate lazy learning' states the learning and integrity worry behind AI guidance, so P41, informs.
units.anchor: compromise student assessments, promote academic dishonesty, and facilitate

units.why: 'it's essential to learn (and perhaps teach) how to write a prompt that works' recommends prompting as a skill, so P44, should, encourage.
units.anchor: it's essential to learn (and perhaps teach) how to write a prompt that works
units.resolution_why: A coded modality informs, B coded actor instructor and modality should. 'essential to learn' is a recommendation, so should; it addresses learners and teachers alike, so all.

units.why: 'this page will be updated frequently with new resources and advice' commits to revising the guidance, so P54, over-time, informs.
units.anchor: this page will be updated frequently with new resources and advice

units.why: 'AI can help you outline your course, create learning objectives, and suggest assignments' recommends instructor use of AI in course preparation, so P59, before-course, may, encourage.
units.anchor: AI can help you outline your course, create learning objectives, and suggest assignments
units.resolution_why: Both coded P59 before-course may. A coded encourage, B permit; the page presents these uses as recommended, so encourage.

units.why: 'how AI tools can help write, modify, or create question sets' offers AI as an aid to instructor assessment preparation, so P59, before-course, may, encourage.
units.anchor: how AI tools can help write, modify, or create question sets
units.resolution_why: A coded modality may, B coded informs. It is offered as a use faculty can adopt, so may. Stance encourage as for the other instructor-use units.

units.why: 'generate summaries of relevant readings or videos you might want to include for students' suggests instructor use of AI for course content, so P59, may, encourage.
units.anchor: generate summaries of relevant readings or videos you might want to include for students
units.resolution_why: Only A coded it. It is the same kind of instructor-use suggestion that both coders coded elsewhere on the page, so kept.

units.why: 'Feeding it your syllabus, lectures, and an in-depth prompt can help make a personal tutorbot' suggests instructors build a course-specific AI tutor, so P17, before-course, may, encourage.
units.anchor: Feeding it your syllabus, lectures, and an in-depth prompt can help make a personal tutorbot
units.resolution_why: Both coded P17 may encourage. A kept practice problems in the same unit; B split them (next unit).

units.why: 'generate unlimited practice problems' suggests instructors use AI to produce practice material for students, so P14 (AI for practice and study aids), may, encourage.
units.anchor: generate unlimited practice problems
units.resolution_why: Only B split this clause out. It is a distinct use (practice problems vs a tutor bot), so kept.

units.why: 'LLMs can be used to provide initial personalized feedback to your students' suggests AI-assisted feedback by instructors, so P59, may, encourage.
units.anchor: LLMs can be used to provide initial personalized feedback to your students
units.resolution_why: Both coded P59 during-work may. A coded encourage and B permit; the page presents this as a recommended use, so encourage.

units.why: 'creating assessments that emphasize skills where AI tools fall short' tells instructors to redesign assessments around what AI cannot do, so P35, should.
units.anchor: creating assessments that emphasize skills where AI tools fall short

units.why: 'Design tasks and assessments that require creativity, practical application of concepts, and critical thinking' is advice to redesign work around AI, so P35, should.
units.anchor: Design tasks and assessments that require creativity, practical application of concepts, and critical thinking

units.why: 'test intermediate steps in the learning process, instead of just the final product' recommends process-based assessment, which redesigns assessment around AI (P35); P40 (process evidence for misconduct) is narrower.
units.anchor: test intermediate steps in the learning process, instead of just the final product

units.why: 'at a minimum provide clear guidelines about the use of AI-generated content in assignments and assessments' asks instructors to state their AI rules, so P09, course-start, should.
units.anchor: provide clear guidelines about the use of AI-generated content in assignments and assessments

units.why: 'yielding garbled or entirely made-up answers' names hallucination as a risk, the reason to verify AI output, so P31, informs.
units.anchor: yielding garbled or entirely made-up answers

units.why: 'Good AI use involves being aware of, checking for, and making efforts to correct such biases' names bias as a harm and asks users to check for it, so P53, should.
units.anchor: Good AI use involves being aware of, checking for, and making efforts to correct such
units.resolution_why: A coded this sentence as phase during-work, should; B coded the adjacent sentence 'AI adopts the biases...' as informs. The two sentences make one point and the checking duty is the rule, so should, phase general (not tied to a course stage).

units.why: 'Personal data is not supposed to be fed to GenAI models' forbids entering personal data, so P50, must-not, restrict.
units.anchor: Personal data is not supposed to be fed to GenAI models.
units.resolution_why: A coded phase during-work, B coded general; the rule is not tied to a course stage, so general.

units.why: 'you should shift the kind of assignments you are providing students' tells instructors to redesign assignments because AI can be misused, so P35, should.
units.anchor: you should shift the kind of assignments you are providing students

units.why: 'enforce academic dhonesty policies' (sic) tells instructors to enforce integrity rules against AI plagiarism, so P36, when-misuse, should.
units.anchor: enforce academic dhonesty policies
units.resolution_why: Only B split this clause from the assignment-redesign clause. It is a distinct rule (enforcement), so kept.

units.why: 'AI-tutored students performed as well or better' cites evidence on how AI affects learning, so P55, over-time, informs.
units.anchor: AI-tutored students performed as well or better
units.resolution_why: A coded actor all, B coded admin; the evidence is not addressed to an office, so all.

units.why: 'the best place is to start is the Harvard AI Sandbox' recommends a university-provided AI tool to faculty, so P17, before-course, should, encourage.
units.anchor: the best place is to start is the Harvard AI Sandbox
units.resolution_why: A coded instructor before-course should, B coded admin general informs. The sentence advises faculty where to start, so instructor, should; stance encourage.

units.why: 'other existing policies, such as Harvard's Information Security Policy ... also apply to GenAI and the use of LLMs' extends existing university policies to AI, so P56, informs.
units.anchor: other existing policies, such as Harvard's Information Security Policy
units.resolution_why: A coded actor all, B coded instructor; the page addresses faculty using LLMs in class, so instructor. Both coded P56 informs.

units.why: 'it's essential to be aware of the University's guidelines ... and to refer to School-specific policies and resources' directs faculty to the governing guidelines, so P56, before-course, should.
units.anchor: be aware of the University's guidelines designed to ensure responsible and effective use
units.policy: Instructors are to be aware of the University's guidelines for responsible and effective use of LLMs and to refer to School-specific policies and resources.
units.resolution_why: A and B each anchored one half of this single sentence (awareness of university guidelines; referring to school policies), both P56 should before-course. They are one rule (consult the governing guidance), so merged into one unit with a normalized policy.

units.why: 'ensuring that students' work remains original and reflective of their understanding and skills' requires that submitted work be the student's own, so P29, must.
units.anchor: ensuring that students' work remains original and reflective of their understanding and skills

units.why: 'The use of generative AI must align with the principles of honesty, respect, and responsibility' sets the institution's principles for AI use, so P56, must.
units.anchor: must align with the principles of honesty, respect, and responsibility
units.resolution_why: Only B coded it separately. It is a distinct principle from the originality requirement, so kept.

units.why: 'Schools within Harvard allow for the customization of AI usage policies by individual instructors' leaves the rule to each instructor, so P04, may; this is why the document delegates.
units.anchor: Schools within Harvard allow for the customization of AI usage policies by individual instructors
units.resolution_why: A coded instructor before-course may, B coded admin general informs. The sentence grants instructors the choice, so instructor, may.

units.why: 'provided these are clearly communicated' makes instructor-set AI policies conditional on clear communication, so P09, course-start, must.
units.anchor: provided these are clearly communicated
units.resolution_why: Only B coded the condition separately. It is a distinct duty from the permission to customize, so kept.

units.why: 'students and faculty are encouraged to be transparent about the use of generative AI in academic work' recommends disclosure, so P24, should.
units.anchor: students and faculty are encouraged to be transparent about the use of generative AI
units.resolution_why: A coded unit_stance neutral, B coded encourage. Disclosure is a condition on use, not encouragement of AI use, so neutral.

units.why: 'Consider co-creating course-specific norms around the use of generative AI with your students' leaves course norms to the instructor and students, so P04, should.
units.anchor: Consider co-creating course-specific norms around the use of generative AI with your students.

units.why: 'we encourage you to engage with peers and organizations at Harvard' recommends faculty learn about AI from peers, so P63, should.
units.anchor: we encourage you to engage with peers and organizations at Harvard
units.resolution_why: Only A coded it. It is a real recommendation about faculty learning, so kept.

units.why: 'it's crucial to strike a balance between leveraging these tools for educational enhancement and ensuring that they do not compromise educational objectives' is a principle for how instructors respond to AI, so P56, should.
units.anchor: strike a balance between leveraging these tools for educational enhancement
units.resolution_why: Only B coded it. It is a real principle statement, so kept.

units.why: 'Each encourages innovative and thoughtful integration of AI in teaching and learning practices' says the Schools' policies welcome AI use, so P02, informs, encourage.
units.anchor: Each encourages innovative and thoughtful integration of AI in teaching and learning practices
units.resolution_why: Only B coded it. It reports the Schools' stance and is a real policy statement, so kept.

documents.unit: John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences, Computing in Engineering Education
documents.title: Generative AI
documents.summary: A short SEAS service page: the Computing in Engineering Education team offers to support faculty integrating generative AI into computational courses and links to Harvard integrity standards. It sets no student rules.
documents.stance_why: The page says CEE is 'committed to supporting faculty and staff in the effective and responsible integration of Generative AI' and believes G-AI 'can enhance the computational learning environment'; it sets no restriction and hands no decision to instructors, so the stance is encourage.

units.why: 'committed to supporting faculty and staff in the effective and responsible integration of Generative AI' commits SEAS CEE to support faculty with AI, so P63, informs, encourage.
units.anchor: committed to supporting faculty and staff in the effective and responsible integration of Generative AI
units.resolution_why: A coded phase before-course, B coded general; a standing commitment is not tied to a stage, so general.

units.why: 'believe that it can enhance the computational learning environment at SEAS' states a welcoming SEAS stance on G-AI, so P02, informs, encourage.
units.anchor: believe that it can enhance the computational learning environment at SEAS
units.resolution_why: A coded P44 (teach AI as a skill), B coded P02. The sentence welcomes AI in the learning environment and does not teach or recommend a skill, so P02.

units.why: 'computational-related course activities, lectures, homework assignments, projects, and labs' sets the scope of the G-AI integration support, so P61.
units.anchor: computational-related course activities, lectures, homework assignments, projects, and labs
units.resolution_why: Only B coded it. It defines scope, so kept. B's mission-statement clause 'empowering and encouraging using state-of-the-art computational tools' was dropped: it speaks of computational tools in general, not AI use.

units.why: 'Interested faculty and staff should contact CEE to request a consultation' offers faculty support for AI integration, so P63, before-course; it is an option for interested faculty, so may.
units.anchor: Interested faculty and staff should contact CEE to request a consultation.

units.why: 'to ensure that students and faculty adhere to Harvard academic integrity standards and best practices' points students and faculty to the university's AI guidelines, so P56, should.
units.anchor: ensure that students and faculty adhere to Harvard academic integrity standards and best practices
units.resolution_why: A coded modality informs and B coded should, with topics integrity-sanctions and policy-evolution. The links exist so users adhere to the standards, so should; topic integrity.

notes: Reconciled from Coder A and Coder B. The university-wide provost, HUIT and FAS pages returned Access Denied and were not coded, so the university layer is represented by the harvard.edu/ai teaching page. No computing-unit or course documents. Two UNCOVERED units: (1) collaborative assignments must list team members; (2) FAS will not provide or license internet-blocking exam proctoring tools. Sample-policy sentences repeated across the three OUE templates (misconduct, acknowledge-and-cite, student validity duty, course-specific expectations) are coded once.
